craft_notes: Sthāyin: collapse-conditional (if-then that eats itself). Rows: row 2 (unreal→not-real). Close: such (īdṛśam as the dismissive closer). Rejected: 'means justify ends' moral — killed: kept conditional (the logic IS the verse); 'that is false' — kept not-real-nor-such (double denial kept).

lines: If non-rejection first is how you reach the real, that is just unreal —
if the unreal then counts as real, that is not real, nor such.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yady atattvaparihārapūrvakaṃ tattvam eṣi tad atattvam eva hi | yady atattvam atha tattvam eva vātattvam eva na tu tattvam īdṛśam

reads_against.argmap: What follows from the condition? → Conditional refutation: mediated attainment collapses into its means; identity-claims about tattva fail both ways.
c1_essence: Reality reached only by first rejecting non-reality is that non-reality; non-reality claimed as reality is neither.
